title: FAA Part 450 Operator Transition
summary: The FAA reports that commercial launch and reentry operators completed transition to Part 450 licensing by the March 2026 deadline and that the agency had issued 14 Part 450 licenses since March 2021.
key_findings: Part 450 became the common current licensing framework for covered commercial launch and reentry operations.
The FAA reported 14 licenses issued under the framework since March 2021.
Framework transition and aggregate license counts do not establish approval, readiness, availability, or performance for a named Space Coast mission.
why_it_matters: The record establishes the national licensing context in which project-specific Space Coast decisions must now be read.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a current regulatory-framework boundary to the Florida shelf.
Directs readers from aggregate transition claims to operator-specific dockets.
Supports later comparison of license, mission, infrastructure, and outcome records.
evidence_limits: The announcement does not list or validate readiness for every named operator or mission.
A Part 450 license is not site availability, range clearance, launch success, or safety performance.
Aggregate license counts should not be presented as launch cadence.
